# KBD Constraints — Kubo

Generated by `/kbd-init` on 2026-10-09 from `AGENTS.md` (Stability, User Agency, Building, Testing, Scope and Safety) and the `kubo-ipfs-agentic` team ownership. `AGENTS.md` remains authoritative; if this file and `AGENTS.md` disagree, `AGENTS.md` wins and this file is regenerated.

Command policy (from `AGENTS.md`), applied to every command below:

- Build with `make build`, never `go build`.
- Integration tests (`test/cli`) require `make build` first, then `PATH="$PWD/cmd/ipfs:$PATH"` and an isolated `IPFS_PATH`. Every `test/cli` command below carries that prefix.
- Dependency changes go through `go get` plus `make mod_tidy` (root, `docs/examples/kubo-as-a-library`, `test/dependencies`).
- Do not run `make test` or `make test_sharness` unless asked.

Path ownership exceptions: `.agent-team/`, `.prometheus/`, `.kbd-orchestrator/`, `.agents/`, `.claude/`, `.codex/`, `.kimi-code/`, `.opencode/` and `openspec/` are deliberately tracked tool and team state, not disposable. `.agents/skills/` holds vendored third-party skills recorded in `.agents/skills/VENDORED.md`.

---

## Blocking Constraints (prevent archiving until resolved)

```yaml
constraints:
  - id: build-passes
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Kubo builds with the Makefile ldflags'
    command: 'make build'

  - id: go-fmt
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Go sources are gofmt-clean'
    command: 'make test_go_fmt'

  - id: lint-passes
    severity: blocking
    description: 'golangci-lint passes via the Makefile target'
    command: 'make -O test_go_lint'

  - id: unit-tests-pass
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Unit tests pass (excludes test/cli)'
    command: 'make test_unit'

  - id: go-mod-in-sync
    severity: blocking
    description: 'All three go.mod files are tidy and on the same dependency versions'
    command: "make mod_tidy && git diff --exit-code -- go.mod go.sum docs/examples/kubo-as-a-library/go.mod docs/examples/kubo-as-a-library/go.sum test/dependencies/go.mod test/dependencies/go.sum"

  - id: no-external-replace-directive
    severity: blocking
    description: 'No committed replace directive pointing at boxo or any external module. In-repo replaces of github.com/ipfs/kubo or its sub-modules (github.com/ipfs/kubo/...) to a relative path are allowed'
    check: "grep -nE '^replace|=>' go.mod docs/examples/kubo-as-a-library/go.mod test/dependencies/go.mod mcp/*/go.mod 2>/dev/null | grep -vE 'github\\.com/ipfs/kubo(/[^ ]*)? => \\.'"

  - id: rpc-api-compatible
    severity: blocking
    description: 'No /api/v0 endpoint removed or renamed, no field renamed, no default changed, no response shape altered; same for core/coreiface interfaces'
    note: 'Manual review of core/commands, core/coreiface, client/rpc diffs; additive endpoints and optional arguments only'

  - id: gateway-conformance
    severity: blocking
    description: 'HTTP Gateway behavior stays spec-conformant'
    command: 'make build && PATH="$PWD/cmd/ipfs:$PATH" IPFS_PATH="$(mktemp -d)" go test ./test/cli/... -run "TestGateway" -v'
    note: 'CI also runs ipfs/gateway-conformance; never weaken its assertions'

  - id: default-cid-recipe-unchanged
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Default ipfs add recipe still matches unixfs-v0-2015'
    command: 'make build && PATH="$PWD/cmd/ipfs:$PATH" IPFS_PATH="$(mktemp -d)" go test ./test/cli/... -run "TestDefaultMatchesExpectedProfile" -v'

  - id: telemetry-opt-outs
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Telemetry honors IPFS_TELEMETRY=off, DO_NOT_TRACK and config opt-out; no new reporting path'
    command: 'make build && PATH="$PWD/cmd/ipfs:$PATH" IPFS_PATH="$(mktemp -d)" go test ./test/cli/... -run "TestTelemetry" -v'

  - id: no-silent-cid-injection
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Announcements follow local actions and Provide.Strategy; Provide.Enabled=false silences them. No feature (including MCP tools) adds, pins or provides CIDs without an operator-initiated local cause'
    command: 'make build && PATH="$PWD/cmd/ipfs:$PATH" IPFS_PATH="$(mktemp -d)" go test ./test/cli/... -run "TestProvider" -v'

  - id: no-tracking
    severity: blocking
    description: 'No code collects, logs or reports who runs a node, what it stores or requests, or whom it connects to; no deanonymization helpers'
    note: 'Manual review; applies to mcp/ server logging and MCP App views'

  - id: configurable-endpoints
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Every hardcoded URL, bootstrap peer, router, CA or shared service is configurable and can be turned off'
    check: "grep -rnE 'https?://' mcp/server mcp/app/src mcp/ui/src --include='*.go' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' 2>/dev/null | grep -vE '_test\\.go|\\.test\\.tsx?|localhost|127\\.0\\.0\\.1|//\\s'"
    note: 'Each hit needs a config override and an off switch documented in docs'

  - id: feature-off-switch
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Every new feature or flipped default has an off switch, a docs/config.md (or mcp docs) entry, a changelog example, and tests with it disabled'
    note: 'Manual review at phase boundary'

  - id: no-resource-appropriation
    severity: blocking
    description: 'No default spending of operator CPU, bandwidth or storage for third parties; no monetization, crypto integration or decentralized-compute features without a prior AGENTS.md policy PR'
    note: 'Manual review'

  - id: protocol-change-needs-ipip
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Any wire/protocol change links an IPIP in ipfs/specs first'
    note: 'Manual review of bitswap, DHT, identify and other wire behavior'

  - id: protected-paths
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Do not modify test/sharness/lib/, .github/ (unless asked), auto-generated Changelog/Contributors sections in docs/changelogs/, version.go or release tooling'
    check: "git diff --name-only HEAD -- test/sharness/lib .github version.go bin/mkreleaselog"

  - id: no-new-sharness-tests
    severity: blocking
    description: 'New integration tests go in test/cli/, not test/sharness/'
    check: "git diff --name-only --diff-filter=A HEAD -- test/sharness"

  - id: no-hardcoded-secrets
    severity: blocking
    description: 'No hardcoded API keys, tokens or passwords; RPC credentials come from env or config'
    check: "grep -rnE '(api[_-]?key|secret|token|password)\\s*[:=]\\s*[\"\\x27][A-Za-z0-9_\\-]{12,}' mcp core cmd client config --include='*.go' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' 2>/dev/null | grep -v _test"

  - id: mcp-tool-annotations
    severity: blocking
    description: 'Every MCP tool declares readOnlyHint/destructiveHint/idempotentHint/openWorldHint matching mcp/contract; destructive tools follow the opt-in ADR'
    note: 'Verified by mcp/server contract tests once they exist'
```

## ADDENDUM: ipfs-mcp-server (G9-G12)

### Summary of findings

1. **None of G9-G12 exists in Kubo, and none of them has to.** The Universal Agent Runtime (UAR, MIT, `uar:LICENSE:1`, `uar:Cargo.toml:35`) already has most of the parts:
   - an agent loop;
   - an OpenAI-compatible LLM client over liter-llm, configurable `base_url` and env-sourced keys;
   - an MCP client over stdio and Streamable HTTP;
   - Cedar plus a tool-approval pause;
   - an AG-UI SSE profile;
   - an A2A JSON-RPC server;
   - local FastEmbed embeddings;
   - SurrealDB in embedded (surrealkv) and remote modes;
   - knowledge-base ingest and search APIs.

   With that, Kubo can keep its side of G9-G12 to MCP tools, the contract and documentation. That matches the AGENTS.md split: Kubo is the daemon and product, and generic capability lives elsewhere.
2. **UAR is not conformant enough to be used as-is.** These defects are verified and land directly on G9 and G11:
   - **A2A.**
     - The agent card is at `/.well-known/agent.json` (`uar:src/uar/api/a2a/mod.rs:75`). A2A 1.0 specifies `/.well-known/agent-card.json` [external].
     - `TaskState` uses `rename_all = "lowercase"` (`uar:src/uar/api/a2a/types.rs:118`), so `InputRequired` goes on the wire as `"inputrequired"`.
     - There is no `auth-required` state, no `message/stream`, and no push notifications (`agent_card.rs:28-29`) [sub].
     - Tool approval never surfaces as A2A input-required: the only mapping arm (`RunStatus::Paused`) is never assigned [sub].
   - **AG-UI.**
     - There is no `RunAgentInput` POST endpoint (grep: 0 hits).
     - There are no spec interrupts. Approval goes out as a `CUSTOM` event, `uar.tool.approval_required` (`uar:src/uar/api/adapters.rs:361-381`), and the decision comes back on a UAR-specific REST endpoint [sub].
   - **MCP client.** It has no elicitation support (grep: 0 hits in `src`) and no MCP Apps `ui://` support (0 hits). This lands on the F4 confirmation gate (see G9 Facts).
   - **CORS.** CORS is `allow_origin(Any)` (`uar:src/server.rs:2528-2533`). A browser chat in the admin-privileged Web UI origin must not depend on that.
3. **UAR's own defaults conflict with the Kubo rules if they are passed straight to users.**
   - The default model is `openai/gpt-4o` (`uar:src/config.rs:1476`), an implicit default endpoint.
   - The default bind is `0.0.0.0:1906` (`uar:src/config.rs:1411-1412`).
   - The dev configs disable JWT (`config.embedded.yaml:19`) [sub].

   Kubo-side material (docs, example configs, plugin manifests) must never ship those defaults.
4. **G12 must not embed SurrealDB into the `ipfs` binary.**
   - The only embedded path from Go is `github.com/surrealdb/surrealdb.c.go`, described as "Go bindings for embedded SurrealDB via the surrealdb.c C FFI library" [external, https://github.com/surrealdb/surrealdb.c.go, fetched 2026-10-09]. That means cgo plus a Rust native library.
   - Kubo has no cgo today: `grep -rln 'import "C"' --include=*.go .` (excluding tests) returns nothing.
   - SurrealDB is licensed "Business Source License 1.1", with "Change License: Apache License, Version 2.0" [external, https://github.com/surrealdb/surrealdb/blob/main/LICENSE, fetched 2026-10-09]. Kubo is MIT/Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE`).
   - The official Go SDK `surrealdb.go` connects to a server over ws/http (`FromEndpointURLString(ctx, "ws://localhost:8000")`) [external, https://surrealdb.com/docs/languages/golang, fetched 2026-10-09].
5. **G11 cannot reuse `mcp/ui` (React 19) inside the Web UI (React 16) by import.**
   - The Web UI is React 16.14 on CRA 5 with Tachyons (`webui:package.json:83, 91, 100, 104`). React is forced to 16 via `overrides` (`:313-314`).
   - It still uses `ReactDOM.render` (`webui:src/index.js:35`) [sub], which React 19 removed.
   - At least eleven dependencies cap peer React at 16 [sub, from `webui:package-lock.json`].

   An upgrade is a rewrite-sized change in a fork that tracks a frequently releasing upstream. An isolated React 19 island is the realistic path.

## ARCHITECTURE OPTIONS

### Facts that constrain every G9-G12 option

1. **The F4 boundary.** `ipfs mcp` is a local command that talks to the daemon only over `/api/v0` and never opens the repo (`assessment.md` DECISION). The daemon, `config/` and `docs/config.md` do not change in this phase (`plan.md` Scope cuts). Every option that adds a daemon listener reopens C1/F1 and needs `docs/config.md` keys, a changelog entry and disabled-state tests (AGENTS.md "Every new feature has an off switch").
2. **Kubo rules that apply directly to G10-G12.**
   - No hardcoded endpoints; every endpoint must be configurable with an off switch.
   - No tracking.
   - No silent CID injection.
   - No resource appropriation.

   Sending node content to an LLM or a remote embedder is data leaving the machine. It is not telemetry, but it carries the same visibility duty: off unless configured, the destination named, and never a default.
3. **The confirmation gate and the token-fallback weakness.** Writes and destructive tools need confirmation on every transport (`operator-answers.md` 5). The gate uses elicitation when the client supports it and a two-step confirm token otherwise. The token proves that the agent asked twice, not that a human agreed (`plan.md` T2).
4. **UAR as an MCP client.**
   - It spawns stdio servers (`uar:src/mcp/registry.rs:693`) or connects to Streamable HTTP (`:720-723`).
   - It is configured in `mcp.json` under `mcpServers`, with `headers` taking `{secret_ref: "env:VAR"}` (`uar:src/mcp/config.rs:10-12, 45-83`).
   - It never forwards its inbound bearer (`uar:docs/configuration.md:308`).
   - It treats every MCP tool as `ApprovalClass::Required` ("MCP annotations are untrusted", `uar:src/mcp/registry.rs:166-167`), so each call through UAR pauses for a human decision (`uar:src/uar/runtime/manager.rs:5496-5508`).
   - It does not implement elicitation.
   - **Consequence:** through UAR, the `ipfs mcp` gate always takes the token fallback. The human gate that actually holds is UAR's own approval pause, which is stronger than T2 because UAR asks a human for every call. A write then takes two approvals: one for the first call, which only returns `confirmation_required`, and one for the confirming call.
5. **Protocol versions** [external, fetched 2026-10-09]:
   - **A2A.** `a2aproject/A2A` `docs/specification.md` is at version 1.0.0. Agent card at `/.well-known/agent-card.json`. Task states include `TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED` and `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED`. Bindings are JSON-RPC, gRPC and HTTP+JSON. Security schemes are API key, HTTP auth, OAuth2, OIDC and mTLS. The release date "Sep 29, 2026" came from an LLM-extracted summary and is [unverified].
   - **A2A Go SDK.** `github.com/a2aproject/a2a-go/v2` exists (https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-go).
   - **AG-UI.** The run is interrupt-aware: `RUN_FINISHED` carries `outcome: {type: "interrupt", interrupts: [...]}`, and the client resumes with a new run whose input carries `resume: [{interruptId, status, payload}]` (https://docs.ag-ui.com/concepts/interrupts, https://docs.ag-ui.com/concepts/events).
   - **AG-UI Go SDK.** Listed as a community SDK (https://docs.ag-ui.com/introduction).
6. **go-sdk can reach the host's LLM without an LLM client.** It has `ServerSession.CreateMessage` and `CreateMessageWithTools` for MCP sampling and `Elicit` (`$GOMODCACHE/github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk@v1.8.0/mcp/server.go:1664, 1710, 1729`). Sampling is not a G10 backend: it only exists inside an MCP host, and the browser chat has none. It is still a zero-dependency way for a stdio host's own model to help, so it is noted here for later.
7. **The Web UI origin is admin-privileged.** It is served on the RPC origin and holds admin RPC (`assessment.md` G8 fact 1, `core/corehttp/webui.go:93-147`). Kubo sets no CSP for it (`grep -rn "Content-Security-Policy" core/ config/ docs/config.md` returns nothing). The Web UI `public/index.html` has no CSP meta [sub]. Desktop sets no CSP and runs `webSecurity: false` (`desktop:src/webui/index.js:41-47`). Anything that loads into that origin runs with admin RPC.

### G9: AG-UI and A2A endpoints

**Options.**

- **(a) Inside the `ipfs mcp` process, beside Streamable HTTP.**
  - Add `/agui` (SSE) and `/a2a` plus `/.well-known/agent-card.json` to the `--http` listener.
  - It reuses the `AuthVerifier`, the scope-to-group map and the confirmation gate in-process: an AG-UI interrupt or an A2A input-required maps one-to-one to a pending confirmation.
  - It needs an agent loop and an LLM client in Go (G10), plus two protocol SDKs (a2a-go v2 and a community AG-UI Go SDK) in the root `go.mod`, on top of go-sdk.
- **(b) A daemon-hosted listener.** This is C1 again (`Addresses.AGUI`/`Addresses.A2A`), with the same rejection grounds as `assessment.md` C1, and worse: it would put an LLM client inside the daemon process.
- **(c) A separate service or binary in this repo** (for example `ipfs-agent`, in its own module). It keeps the root module clean but grows a second product in the Kubo repo with its own release tooling (`assessment.md` option B costs). It still needs the Go loop and LLM client.
- **(d) Hosted by UAR, which calls IPFS through `ipfs mcp` as a tool provider.**
  - UAR serves AG-UI and A2A and owns the loop, the model, approvals and sessions.
  - `ipfs mcp` (stdio spawn or `--http` with a bearer token) is one entry in UAR's `mcp.json`.
  - Kubo adds no protocol endpoint. Its part is the contract, an example UAR configuration, docs and real-service tests.
  - The UAR gaps (Summary 2) are fixed in UAR.
- **(e1) A hybrid: (d) plus an LLM-free A2A facade in `ipfs mcp`.** An A2A `DataPart` `{tool, arguments}` maps to one contract tool. Confirmation maps to input-required. There is no model. This gives agent-to-agent delegation of deterministic IPFS operations without any LLM.
- **(e2) A hybrid: (d) now, (a) later as a fallback** if the operator rejects the UAR dependency. Both reuse the same contract, so the fallback costs no redesign.

**How each option reuses the shared pieces:**

| Option | Contract reuse | Auth reuse | Confirmation-gate reuse |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) | Direct, in-process | Same `AuthVerifier` in-process | Native: one pending-confirmation object, rendered as an AG-UI interrupt or A2A input-required |
| (b) | Direct | A second auth system in the daemon | Native, but inside the daemon |
| (c) | Generated copy | Duplicated verifier | Duplicated gate |
| (d) | Through MCP `tools/list`; UAR reads names, schemas and annotations | UAR authenticates its own clients (JWT/API key, `uar:src/uar/security/middleware.rs:168-199`) [sub]; UAR authenticates to `ipfs mcp` with the static bearer, mapped to scopes by `AuthVerifier` | Two gates: UAR's approval pause (human, every call) plus the `ipfs mcp` token fallback (agent). See the decision risks. |
| (e1) | Direct | Same verifier | Native, input-required |

**Scores** (1 worst, 5 best; "Kubo surface" is 5 when nothing new is added to Kubo):

| Option | Goal fit | Kubo surface | Rules fit (no default endpoint, off switch) | Security | Maintenance in this repo | Time to working result | Interop/conformance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) in `ipfs mcp` | 5 | 2 | 4 | 4 | 1 | 2 | 4 (we control conformance) |
| (b) daemon listener | 4 | 1 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 4 |
| (c) separate binary | 4 | 3 | 4 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 4 |
| **(d) UAR-hosted** | **4** | **5** | **4** | **4** | **5** | **4** | **2 now, 4 after UAR fixes** |
| (e1) LLM-free A2A facade | 2 | 3 | 5 | 4 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| (e2) (d) now, (a) as fallback | 4 | 5 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 4 | 2 to 4 |

### G10: LLM backend

**Options.**

- **(L1) UAR is the only agent loop.** The operator points UAR either at its own provider config or at "an OpenAI-compatible server plus key", which UAR already supports:
  - `--llm-base-url`/`LLM_BASE_URL` and `--llm-api-key`/`LLM_API_KEY` (`uar:src/config.rs:50, 54`);
  - YAML `providers: {base_url, api_key: "${ENV}"}` (`uar:docs/configuration.md:246-259`) [sub].

  The "OpenAI-compatible" choice is then a UAR configuration, not a second code path in Kubo.
- **(L2) Minimal Go loop in `ipfs mcp`** for the OpenAI-compatible case, with UAR as the other option. It adds:
  - a chat-completions client (stream parsing and tool-call assembly);
  - a loop with step and budget limits;
  - session storage;
  - prompt and system-prompt management;
  - tool-result truncation;
  - AG-UI/A2A event emission.

  That is a second agent runtime to keep correct, written in a repo whose maintainers' stated scope is the daemon.
- **(L3) Proxy only.** Kubo forwards AG-UI/A2A to an operator-configured UAR URL. It adds a hop and an auth translation and solves nothing that pointing clients straight at UAR does not.
- **(L4) MCP sampling** (fact 6). This is a supplement for stdio hosts only and is not a G10 backend.

**Where the loop lives when "OpenAI-compatible" is chosen: in UAR (L1).** Requiring UAR is acceptable only if UAR is easy for an operator to run locally.

- **Native installers:** `uar:packaging/native/{macos,linux,windows}`.
- **Docker image:** `ghcr.io/prometheus-ags/universal-agent-runtime`.
- **The cost is a second install.** Prebuilt standalone binaries are published only for `uar-sidecar` [sub]. That is the main weakness of L1 (see Risks).

**Rules applied to G10, whichever option is chosen:**

- There is no default endpoint. Kubo docs and the example configs set a provider explicitly, and they show `UAR_LOCAL_ONLY` (`uar:src/llm/local_only.rs:20, 25-26`) [sub] as the recommended start for local models.
- Keys come from env or a secret file, never a config literal. UAR's `${ENV}` and `secret_ref: "env:VAR"` forms are the only ones shown.
- The feature is off unless configured. Nothing in Kubo starts UAR or contacts it on its own.
- Data egress is visible. When an agent reads node content (`ipfs_cat`, `ipfs_get`, `dag_get`), that content reaches whatever model UAR uses.

**Scores:**

| Option | Goal fit | Kubo surface | Rules fit | Maintenance | Operator setup cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **L1 UAR loop for both backends** | **4** | **5** | **4** | **5** | **2** (a second runtime to install) |
| L2 Go loop + UAR | 5 | 1 | 4 | 1 | 4 |
| L3 proxy in Kubo | 3 | 2 | 3 | 3 | 2 |
| L4 sampling only | 1 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 |

### G11: chat UI in Desktop and the Web UI

**Compatibility problem, concretely.** All facts here are [sub] with lead spot-checks.

- **The Web UI:**
  - React 16.14 and CRA 5 via `react-app-rewired-esm`;
  - Tachyons and `ipfs-css` for styling, no Tailwind;
  - TypeScript 4.x, Storybook 6.5 and Enzyme with the React 16 adapter;
  - `ReactDOM.render` at `webui:src/index.js:35`;
  - a class-component shell with the legacy `DropTarget` HOC (`webui:src/App.js:9, 127`).
- **Peers capped at React 16:** `@tableflip/react-dropdown`, `react-ace` 8, `react-country-flag` 1, `react-popper-tooltip` 2, `react-textarea-autosize` 7, `simplebar-react` 1, `@reach/router` 1.3.4, and others.
- **Peers capped at React 17 and 18:** `react-hook-form` 6, `react-chartjs-2` 2, `react-virtualized`, `react-joyride` 2.9, Storybook 6.5.
- **shadcn/ui on Tailwind 4 assumes React 19 and Tailwind's preflight.** Preflight would restyle every Tachyons element if it loaded globally.

**Options.**

- **(U1) Upgrade the Web UI fork to React 19, Tailwind 4 and shadcn.** That means replacing or upgrading about 20 dependencies, CRA, Storybook and Enzyme, and rewriting the shell. It is a large divergence from upstream `ipfs/ipfs-webui`, which releases frequently via semantic-release (`assessment.md` Risk 9). It would make every later upstream rebase expensive.
- **(U2) A React 19 island.**
  - **What it is.** A self-contained bundle (React 19 + Tailwind 4 + shadcn + the A2UI renderer from `mcp/ui`), exported as a custom element (`<ipfs-agent-chat>`) with a shadow root, so Tailwind's preflight and tokens cannot leak into Tachyons. The reverse holds too.
  - **Mounting.** The Web UI mounts it next to `<Notify/>` in the shell (`webui:src/App.js:63-106`) behind a Settings toggle that is off by default. Two React copies load; the new one only when the toggle is on (dynamic import). The bundle is built in-tree and copied into the Web UI build, never fetched remotely.
  - **Desktop.** Desktop gets it for free through the bundled Web UI (D1, `desktop:package.json:24`).
- **(U3) Desktop-only sidebar.**
  - **What it is.** An Electron `WebContentsView` or a second renderer hosting the React 19 chat beside the Web UI. Desktop has no React today; a new renderer, preload and IPC would be added.
  - **Reach.** Browser users of `/webui` get nothing.
  - **Security.** The chat can run in a separate, non-admin origin. That is the best security property of any option.
- **(U4) Iframe UAR's own React 19 operator UI** (`uar:README.md:13`) [sub] into a side panel.
  - **Fit.** It is not IPFS-specific and not Promethity-branded, and it does not use the shared A2UI catalog.
  - **CORS and auth.** It needs CORS framing changes in UAR and cross-origin auth.

**How the chat reaches AG-UI (applies to U2 and U3).**

- **Endpoint.** The UAR base URL is an operator setting in the chat panel; there is no default. The browser calls UAR directly. Kubo's RPC origin never proxies it, so no new Kubo route and no CORS change on the RPC port.
- **CORS.** UAR must allow only the specific origins: `http://127.0.0.1:5001`, `http://localhost:5001`, `webui://localhost`, and any subdomain-gateway origin used in D3. Its current `allow_origin(Any)` (`uar:src/server.rs:2528-2533`) is not acceptable for a credentialed browser client. That is a UAR change.
- **Auth from the browser.**
  - **Web UI.** A UAR API key (`X-API-Key`, `uar:src/uar/security/middleware.rs:168-172`) [sub] scoped to chat. It is held in memory or per-origin `localStorage`, the same trust level the Web UI already gives the RPC address. Any script on the admin origin can read it; the admin origin can already do far more.
  - **Desktop.** It can do better: the preload can hold the key through Electron `safeStorage` and attach it from main. That needs a new IPC method (today the bridge exposes only `countly*`, consent and `updateLanguage`, `desktop:src/webui/preload.js:55-90`) [sub].
- **CSP.** Neither the Web UI nor Desktop sets one (fact 7). The island must not need `unsafe-eval` or remote assets. The Desktop fork should add a CSP header for `webui://localhost` whose `connect-src` lists the RPC address and the configured UAR origin. That is a Desktop-fork change.
- **Confirmation in chat.** UAR approval requests arrive as the AG-UI `CUSTOM` event `uar.tool.approval_required` (`uar:src/uar/api/adapters.rs:361-381`). The island renders them with the confirmation dialog from `mcp/ui` and answers via `POST /api/uar/runs/{run_id}/tool-approval` [sub]. Once UAR emits spec interrupts, the island switches to `RUN_FINISHED` interrupt outcomes plus `resume`.

**Brand.** PRODUCT.md applies Promethity in full to agent-facing surfaces but leaves open "how far the Promethity identity is applied inside the ipfs-webui fork". Inside a shadow-root island the brand can be applied fully without touching Web UI styles. That is a reason to prefer U2, and the open decision is put to the operator (question 6).

**Ownership.**

- ui-ux-engineer owns `mcp/ui/**` and `mcp/app/**`. Neither the island path nor the Web UI mount path is granted. The plan grants only `src/webmcp/**` in the Web UI fork (`plan.md` change 0).
- No role owns the Desktop fork (`tribe-health/ipfs-desktop`) at all.
- New grants are required: `mcp/chat/**` and Web UI `src/agent-chat/**` for ui-ux-engineer, and Desktop `src/webui/preload.js` plus CSP for an assigned role after operator approval.

**Scores:**

| Option | Goal fit | Upstream-rebase cost (5 = low) | Security | Reach | Effort (5 = low) | Brand control |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| U1 upgrade the fork | 5 | 1 | 3 | 5 | 1 | 3 |
| **U2 React 19 island in the Web UI (reaches Desktop via D1)** | **5** | **4** | **3** | **5** | **3** | **5** |
| U3 Desktop-only side view | 3 | 5 | 5 | 2 | 3 | 5 |
| U4 iframe UAR UI | 2 | 4 | 2 | 4 | 4 | 1 |

### G12: embeddings into SurrealDB

**Verified constraints.**

- **SurrealDB from Go** (Summary 4):
  - Embedded mode needs cgo plus a native library via `surrealdb.c.go`.
  - The pure-Go SDK is a network client.
  - The engine is BSL 1.1.
  - Kubo has zero cgo today.
- **UAR already provides:**
  - surrealkv embedded storage by default (`uar:src/config.rs:1439-1440`, `surrealkv://./data/uar.db`) and remote ws/http (`config.remote.surreal.yaml:12, 30-37`) [sub];
  - FastEmbed BGE-small-en-v1.5 (384 dimensions), loaded from committed local weights with no hub download at runtime (`uar:src/uar/rag/embeddings/fastembed.rs:49-55, 87-101`) [sub];
  - remote embedders: OpenAI, Voyage and Cohere (`uar:src/uar/rag/embeddings/mod.rs:104-118`) [sub];
  - chunking (`uar:src/uar/rag/chunking.rs:27-44`);
  - per-knowledge-base upload and search (`uar:src/uar/api/knowledge.rs:155-169`) [sub].
- **UAR weaknesses relevant to G12** [sub]:
  - Knowledge search computes cosine similarity in memory over loaded chunks, with no HNSW index (`uar:src/uar/persistence/providers/surreal.rs:1738-1739, 2073`). HNSW exists only in the vendored memory server.
  - `/api/ingest` hardcodes the "default" knowledge base.
  - The memory subsystem defaults to OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` (`uar:src/config.rs:1464-1465`), so the remote embedder is a default there.
  - `fastembed` builds with `ort-download-binaries`, which fetches ONNX Runtime at build time (`uar:Cargo.toml:450-455`).
  - The SurrealDB features beyond `kv-surrealkv` (`mem://`, `rocksdb://`, `http`) are [unverified].
- **Kubo has no GC or unpin event stream.** Nothing pushes "CID removed" to a consumer. Deletion can only follow agent-initiated `pin_rm`/`repo_gc` calls or a reconciliation pass using `pin_ls`.

**Options.**

- **(E1) UAR owns everything: embedding, store and search.**
  - **Trigger.** Ingestion happens only through the agent surfaces: a UAR-side tool or flow that ingests bytes the agent just added with `ipfs_add` (or fetched with `ipfs_cat`), keyed by CID.
  - **Settings.** Content types, chunking, model and dimension are UAR settings.
  - **Kubo side.** Contract metadata only (which tools carry content, and its CID and MIME type) plus docs.
- **(E2) `ipfs mcp` embeds via surrealdb.c.go (cgo).** Rejected on cgo, the BSL license and the native-library distribution, on top of the scope argument.
- **(E3) `ipfs mcp` manages a SurrealDB sidecar** (`surreal start file:` or memory) and treats it as "embedded". Kubo would supervise a third-party BSL server process, choose its ports, and add a remote client plus an embedding client. That is resource use and process management Kubo does not do today.
- **(E4) A different store inside Kubo**, such as a pure-Go vector index in a new datastore. It misses the goal's SurrealDB requirement and grows a vector store in Kubo.
- **(E5) A daemon-wide hook** that embeds everything added. This is **refused**, not just rejected. It processes all node content, including CIDs fetched for others, without a per-item local cause. It breaks User Agency ("No silent CID injection" in spirit, and "Never appropriate the machine's resources") and the no-tracking rule's intent (building an index of what the node stores). There is no flagged variant of this option.

**Scores:**

| Option | Goal fit | Kubo surface | Rules fit | License/build fit | Maintenance | Search quality now |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **E1 UAR owns it** | **4** | **5** | **4** | **4** (BSL in UAR, not in Kubo) | **5** | **2** (in-memory cosine, no ANN index) |
| E2 cgo embedded in `ipfs` | 4 | 1 | 3 | 1 | 1 | 4 |
| E3 sidecar managed by `ipfs mcp` | 4 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 2 | 4 |
| E4 other store in Kubo | 2 | 1 | 3 | 4 | 2 | 3 |
| E5 daemon-wide hook | n/a (refused) | | | | | |

---

## DECISION

One decision per goal. All four share one principle, which is the substance of this addendum: **UAR owns the agent loop, the LLM client, AG-UI/A2A, embeddings and SurrealDB. Kubo's side of G9-G12 is the MCP tools, the contract, documentation and real-service tests. Kubo grows no LLM client, no vector store and no chat backend.**

### G9: (d) UAR-hosted AG-UI and A2A, with `ipfs mcp` as a tool provider (e2: the Go fallback is documented, not built)

1. **Connection.** UAR consumes `ipfs mcp`:
   - **Local:** UAR spawns `ipfs mcp` over stdio. One user, one machine; no bearer needed.
   - **Remote:** UAR connects to `ipfs mcp --http` with the static bearer from a `secret_ref: "env:..."` header. That bearer maps through `AuthVerifier` to a dedicated principal with explicit tool-group scopes.
2. **No new Kubo endpoint.** Kubo adds no AG-UI or A2A endpoint, no daemon listener, no `Addresses.*` key and no `docs/config.md` key. F4 is unchanged.
3. **Contract additions** (`mcp/contract`, architect-owned):
   - per-tool `contentEgress`: does the output contain node content that will reach the agent's model?;
   - per-tool A2A skill metadata (id, tags, examples), so UAR's agent card can advertise the IPFS skills without hand-written copies;
   - an AG-UI/A2UI binding hint per output schema (which `mcp/ui` component renders it).
4. **Confirmation semantics through UAR.**
   - **Today.** The human gate is UAR's per-call approval (`uar:src/mcp/registry.rs:166-167`, `manager.rs:5496-5508`). The `ipfs mcp` token fallback still applies underneath, so a write takes two human approvals in UAR. This is accepted as safe but noisy.
   - **Rejected: skipping the second approval.** Adding a "host-delegated confirmation" scope that lets `ipfs mcp` trust UAR's approval and skip the token is not adopted in this phase. It would make one principal's bearer token enough to bypass the gate.
   - **Planned: MCP elicitation in UAR's client.** Once UAR implements it, `ipfs mcp` uses its primary elicitation path and the double approval disappears.
5. **UAR conformance work is a prerequisite, filed as a cross-team request.** It is not done by this team, and no file in UAR is edited from this phase:
   - the agent card at `/.well-known/agent-card.json` (keep `agent.json` as an alias);
   - the TaskState wire values per A2A 1.0;
   - approval surfaced as `input-required`;
   - `auth-required`;
   - `message/stream`;
   - an AG-UI `RunAgentInput` endpoint and spec interrupts (`RUN_FINISHED` outcome interrupt plus `resume`);
   - a CORS allowlist instead of `Any`;
   - an MCP client that supports elicitation.
6. **Off switch.** UAR is not started, configured or contacted by Kubo. With UAR absent, nothing changes for a Kubo user. On the Kubo side, the operator can also drop the tool groups UAR may use (`--tools`) or not issue it a token.

**Flip conditions:**

| If the operator answers... | ...the G9 decision flips to |
|---|---|
| "No dependency on UAR" or "IPFS must serve AG-UI/A2A itself" | **(a)** in `ipfs mcp --http`: a2a-go v2 and an AG-UI Go implementation in the root module behind a new `noagent` build tag, plus G10 L2 (a Go loop). About 3 new changes and a large Round 5-7 addition. |
| "A2A delegation without any LLM is enough" | **(e1)**: an LLM-free A2A facade in `ipfs mcp`, one change, no G10 work |
| The UAR conformance request is declined or not delivered within this phase | Ship G9 as "UAR-hosted, non-conformant A2A, UAR-profile AG-UI", stated plainly in the docs, or flip to (a) on operator choice. Do not claim A2A or AG-UI conformance. |
| "The daemon must host it" | **Refuse in this phase** (same grounds as `assessment.md` C1/F1); offer (a). |

### G10: L1, UAR is the only agent loop

- **Both G10 backends run through UAR.** "Operator-configured UAR" and "operator-configured OpenAI-compatible server plus key" are two UAR configurations: provider `base_url` plus `api_key: "${ENV}"`. No Go agent loop or LLM client is written in Kubo.
- **Kubo-side deliverables** (docs and examples only, under `mcp/uar/` and `docs/mcp/`):
  - an example `mcp.json` entry for `ipfs mcp`;
  - two example UAR configs, local-only (`UAR_LOCAL_ONLY`, a local OpenAI-compatible server) and remote (operator-named provider);
  - neither example names a default provider, and both set `security.jwt_required: true` and a loopback bind;
  - docs that say plainly that node content an agent reads is sent to the configured model.
- **Data-egress visibility.** The chat UI shows the configured model endpoint host and a "local" or "remote" label, derived from the UAR settings API. Its first use per session shows a one-line notice. This is a UI duty in G11, not a Kubo daemon feature.

**Flip conditions:**

| If... | Then |
|---|---|
| The operator rejects UAR as a dependency | **L2**: a minimal Go loop in `mcp/agent` inside the root module behind `noagent`. It is an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions client only, with configured `base_url` and an env/file key, no default, step and token budgets, and tool calls through the same in-process gate. Add `mcp-agent-loop` plus the G9 (a) changes. |
| The setup cost of UAR proves prohibitive (no prebuilt binary for the operator's platform) | Keep L1 but add a documented Docker-compose path; L2 only if the operator asks. |

### G11: U2, a React 19 chat island in the Web UI fork, reaching Desktop through the bundled Web UI

1. **The `mcp/chat` package** (React 19, Tailwind 4 and shadcn inside a shadow root):
   - It reuses `mcp/ui` components and the A2UI catalog.
   - It includes an AG-UI client for the UAR profile now and spec interrupts later.
   - It exports a custom element and builds to one ESM bundle with no remote fonts, CDNs or analytics (PRODUCT.md constraints). Brand tokens come from the bundled Promethity files.
2. **The Web UI fork mounts it** in the shell behind a Settings toggle, off by default.
   - The UAR URL and API key are entered by the user; there is no default URL.
   - The element is loaded by dynamic import only when the toggle is on.
   - i18n strings go in a new `agentChat` namespace (`webui:src/i18n.js:41`) [sub].
   - Visual changes outside the island are limited to the toggle and the launcher button (PRODUCT.md constraint on the fork).
3. **Desktop gets the island through D1** (`IPFS_WEBUI_PATH`). Desktop-fork changes are a separate, operator-gated change:
   - a `safeStorage`-backed key bridge in the preload;
   - a CSP for `webui://localhost` whose `connect-src` lists the RPC and the configured UAR origin;
   - fixing `webSecurity: false` is out of scope but recorded as a risk.
4. **Tool calls in chat are gated by UAR approval** (every MCP call) and rendered with the shared confirmation dialog. A denied action does not run ("Deny is final.").

**Flip conditions:**

| If... | Then |
|---|---|
| The operator wants the chat outside the admin origin | **U3**: a Desktop-only side view in its own origin. Browser `/webui` users get no chat. |
| The operator commits to a full Web UI modernization | **U1**, as its own multi-change effort, not in this phase |
| The operator wants the IPFS identity, not Promethity, inside the Web UI | U2 is unchanged; only the token set inside the shadow root changes. |

### G12: E1, UAR owns embeddings and SurrealDB; Kubo provides only contract metadata and docs

- **Trigger.** Embedding is triggered only by agent-surface actions, never by the daemon:
  - UAR ingests content that an agent added through `ipfs_add` (bytes it already holds) or explicitly asked to index (an explicit "index this CID" tool on the UAR side).
  - It is subject to an operator-set MIME allowlist (default: text/plain, text/markdown, application/pdf through UAR's existing extractors [unverified which extractors exist]) and a size cap.
- **Storage.** Vectors are stored in a UAR knowledge base dedicated to the node, one record per chunk with `cid`, `path` (if MFS), `mime`, `chunk_index` and `model`, in surrealkv (embedded) or remote SurrealDB.
- **Off by default.** The embedder defaults to local FastEmbed. A remote embedder or remote SurrealDB is an explicit operator choice.
- **Deletion.**
  - When the agent calls `pin_rm` or `repo_gc` through UAR, UAR deletes that CID's vectors after the call succeeds.
  - A reconciliation flow (operator-triggered, or scheduled only if the operator configures it) lists pins through `pin_ls` and deletes vectors for unpinned CIDs.
  - Content unpinned outside the agent (CLI, Web UI) stays searchable until the next reconciliation. This is documented as a limitation.
- **Refused:** any daemon-wide embedding hook (E5).

**Flip conditions:**

| If... | Then |
|---|---|
| The operator rejects UAR | **E3**, a sidecar with `ipfs mcp` as the client, only with explicit approval of process management and the BSL dependency. Or defer G12. Never E2. |
| ANN search quality matters at scale | Fix UAR's knowledge-base search to use an HNSW index (UAR change). No Kubo change. |
| The operator requires immediate deletion on any unpin | That needs a Kubo event source for pin removal, which does not exist. It would be a new RPC feature with config, docs and an off switch, as its own Kubo change. Not in this phase. |

---

## ADR DRAFTS

The plan stage materializes these in `docs/mcp/`. The numbering continues after ADR-0001 to ADR-0003 (`plan.md` change 2).

### ADR-0004 draft: agentic endpoints (AG-UI, A2A) and the LLM backend are hosted by UAR

- **Status:** Proposed. Accepted on operator approval at the plan boundary.
- **Context.**
  - Goals G9 and G10.
  - F4 keeps Kubo's MCP surface in `ipfs mcp`, RPC-only, with no daemon or config change.
  - AGENTS.md forbids default endpoints and requires off switches.
  - UAR (MIT) already has an agent loop, an LLM client with configurable `base_url` and env keys, an MCP client (stdio and Streamable HTTP), Cedar plus approval pauses, an AG-UI SSE profile and an A2A JSON-RPC server (`uar:` citations in the Facts).
  - UAR deviates from A2A 1.0 and AG-UI in the places listed in Summary 2.
  - UAR requires approval for every MCP tool call and does not implement elicitation.
- **Decision.**
  - UAR serves AG-UI and A2A and is the only agent loop, for both the "UAR" and the "OpenAI-compatible server" backends (provider config in UAR).
  - `ipfs mcp` is UAR's IPFS tool provider: stdio locally, `--http` with a scoped static bearer remotely.
  - Kubo adds contract metadata (`contentEgress`, A2A skill metadata, A2UI binding hints), example configs without defaults, docs, and real-service tests.
  - UAR conformance fixes are requested from the UAR team, not made here.
- **Consequences.**
  - **Positive:** no LLM client, protocol SDK or agent runtime in Kubo or its `go.mod`; one gate implementation; G9 and G10 follow UAR's improvements.
  - **Negative:**
    - Operators must install and run UAR, a second runtime.
    - A2A and AG-UI conformance depends on another team's delivery.
    - Writes need two approvals until UAR supports elicitation.
    - UAR's own defaults (OpenAI model, `0.0.0.0`, permissive CORS) must be overridden in every documented setup.
- **Rejected alternatives:**

  | Alternative | Rejected because |
  |---|---|
  | (a) in `ipfs mcp` | Adds a Go agent loop, an LLM client and two protocol SDKs to Kubo's root module. Kept as the documented fallback if UAR is rejected. |
  | (b) daemon listener | Same as `assessment.md` C1, plus an LLM client in the daemon |
  | (c) separate binary in this repo | A second product and its release tooling in the Kubo repo, still with a Go loop |
  | L2 Go loop for the OpenAI-compatible case | Duplicates UAR's runtime; maintenance in the wrong repo |
  | L3 proxy | Adds a hop and an auth translation with no gain |
  | "Host-delegated confirmation" scope | Lets a single bearer bypass the confirmation gate |

### ADR-0005 draft: chat UI as a React 19 island in the Web UI fork

- **Status:** Proposed.
- **Context.**
  - G11.
  - The Web UI is React 16 on CRA 5 with Tachyons, and many dependencies cap React at 16 to 18 (`webui:package.json:83, 91, 100, 104`) [sub].
  - `mcp/ui` targets React 19 and A2UI v0.9.
  - The Web UI origin holds admin RPC.
  - Desktop bundles the Web UI and has no React, no CSP and `webSecurity: false` (`desktop:src/webui/index.js:41-47`).
  - The PRODUCT.md brand is Promethity, and its application inside the fork is an open decision.
- **Decision.**

# Goals

- G1 Architecture decision by assessment with adversarial review: evaluate every placement for MCP support (ipfs CLI subcommand, separate binary/module over the RPC API, daemon-hosted endpoint alongside RPC/gateway, plugin, out-of-tree package, other) against Kubo stability and user-agency rules, security, distribution and maintenance cost; record the chosen option and rejected alternatives as an ADR
- G2 MCP server exposing IPFS operations to agents (add/get/cat, pinning, IPNS publish/resolve and keys, MFS, DAG, CAR import/export, routing/provide, node status) with accurate tool annotations and structured output, driven by one shared tool contract in mcp/contract
- G3 Transports: stdio for local agents and Streamable HTTP for remote use, with authentication, loopback-by-default binding, Origin/DNS-rebinding protection, and an off switch for every capability
- G4 MCP App with UI/UX: React 19 component library that is also an A2UI v0.9 catalog, served as ui:// resources, WCAG 2.2 AA, light and dark
- G5 agentskills.io-compliant skills for push/pull, pinning, IPNS, MFS, DAG/CAR and troubleshooting, packaged as plugins and marketplaces for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Kimi Code
- G6 No break to /api/v0, the HTTP gateway, the default CID recipe or wire compatibility; no tracking; no silent CID injection; destructive operations gated; docs and tests for every feature and its disabled state
- G7 Work is executed by the kubo-ipfs-agentic agent team with independent security and quality review at the phase boundary
